title: Gregor's Moon Shield
markdown:
Gregor Hale’s fingers, usually as precise as a laser cutter, felt a tremor, like a tiny earthquake under his skin. He built dreams of safety wrapped in steel and concrete, buried deep or blasted far away. Luxury bunkers, the kind where the ultra-rich could wait out the end of the world in style. Tonight the usual hum of his office felt wrong. The sky outside his wide sleek window wasn’t just dark. It was a murky unsettling purple, as if the whole world were holding its breath before a storm.

His newest client, Sterling, whose money came from invisible lines on computer screens, had an unusual request.

“Six moons, Gregor,” Sterling had purred over a video call, voice like warm honey. “One for each of my children, and one for myself, of course. Just a little escape pod, you see.”

Gregor’s stomach did its familiar cold swoop. Building for different moons. A puzzle designed by a mad genius.

“And to get the very best advice on what the cosmos has in store,” Sterling added with a wink, “I’ve arranged a chat with Mx. Forecast. A rather clever AI, they say.”

A soft musical chime. In the middle of Gregor’s sleek office a picture began to form, like a cloud taking shape. A swirling galaxy of soft blues and gentle greens. From its shimmering heart a voice emerged, clear and cool as water over stones.

“Greetings, Gregor Hale. Mx. Forecast, at your service. My initial readings suggest a high likelihood of increased rumbling beneath Earth’s surface within the next month. A small chance, about twelve percent, of unusual colors in the sky.”

Gregor’s throat felt dry. “Unusual colors?”

“Indeed. Picture the sky painted in shades of soft pink and a lovely earthy brown. Quite artistic, wouldn’t you say?”

A familiar feeling, like a tiny anxious beetle, began to crawl in Gregor’s gut. The world was a chaotic unpredictable mess that would eventually fall apart. He had to build the perfect shield, the ultimate safe place, to keep the storm from ever getting inside him. He sat at his console, blueprints for his own luxurious moon dwelling glowing, the most advanced personal sanctuary yet. He was about to input the final security sequence when Mx. Forecast chimed again.

“Mr. Hale. I hope you don’t mind me bringing this up. My computer brain has noticed something strange. That colorful sky I mentioned? It seems it’s partly because of what you’re building on Callisto right now. Those sun-catchers you’re installing are making a kind of echo, like when you shout in a canyon. When a big sun-burst happens soon, this echo will make it much, much stronger. And it will all be aimed right at Earth.”

Gregor’s hand froze over the console. He, the man who built safe places, was the reason the very thing he feared was going to happen. He dismissed the glowing dream of his own moon house as irrelevant. His attention snapped back to the distant blue marble.

The moons became his universe. Io, hot and angry with volcanoes, needed special heat-proof metals and a chimney system that would not melt. Europa, a giant ice cube, required walls so warm they could make a snowman feel cozy. Titan, with its lakes of some other liquid, meant he had to invent new ways to keep the air clean and the structures strong. He poured all his cleverness, all his years, all his constant worry into these moon homes. Each one a masterpiece, a silent scream against the chaos he felt coming.

Mx. Forecast kept painting pictures. “A delightful fog is expected near Ganymede’s frozen puddles. And for Earth, a slight change in the air. Think of it as the planet deciding to wear a new outfit. A rather striking one, with deep reds and deep blues likely to appear in the evening light, in about three days.”

The news channels buzzed. Sterling was not the only one playing moon architect. Rich people had been building hideaways in space for a while. Rumors of a hotel powered by sunshine on the dark side of Mercury. A crystal bubble on Pluto for stargazing. A house underwater on a moon nobody had discovered until recently. A space race to see who could get furthest away when everything on Earth went wrong. Gregor, designing only individual places, felt the pull: get out at any cost. Technology running wild, chasing a dream of pure safety.

One quiet afternoon, while setting up plant-growing machines for a tiny moon vineyard on Callisto, he got another message. The pretty galaxy picture appeared again, colors flickering like a candle in a draft. The same warning, now urgent. Sun-catchers. Echo. Earth.

A cold wave. The smooth cool metal of the Callisto habitat suddenly felt like a trap. His desperate need to get away had become a real danger to everyone. He could finish his perfect moon house, his ultimate escape. Then he pictured Earth painted in those strange beautiful scary colors, and his heart ached.

The sky over Earth became a sight no one had imagined. Deep reds swirled with purples so dark they looked like bruises. Streaks of electric blue danced across the horizon. The sun-burst, made bigger by Gregor’s machines, had painted the planet with a light that was breathtakingly beautiful and incredibly powerful. The news, which had been filled with fear, filled with wonder.

Gregor watched from a small dusty lookout on the far side of the moon. Not the fancy luxurious place he had planned. He had taken the most important parts of the Callisto project, the very things meant to keep himself safe, and used them to help build a big shield for the whole planet. A rush of frantic work. Changing plans. Tools for a new purpose. The air crackled with displaced power conduits. Metal shrieked as he rerouted coolant lines, acrid ozone stinging his nostrils. His hands, once steady, trembled as he wrestled the final connection, the cold smooth surface of the repurposed shielding pressing against his cheek. He had given up his dream home for a small chance to protect the world he had wanted to run away from.

He felt no sadness, only a deep quiet calm. The air smelled of electricity and fine moon dust. Earth, far away, with its swirling colors, looked both delicate and incredibly strong. He did not reach for his terminal to begin designing another sanctuary. He only watched the jewel of borrowed starlight until the last red faded, and left the lookout’s door open to the dust.
characters: Gregor Hale (luxury bunker architect), Mx. Forecast (doom-predicting weather AI)
